articleTitle: Optimization Methods for Memory Access Monitoring Based on Hardware Page Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Memory access monitoring is commonly used in memory security, performance optimization, and program debugging. Currently, software instrumentation is the main method for implementing byte-grained memory access monitoring, but there are problems of limited application scenarios or excessive performance overhead. Meanwhile, hardware-based memory access monitoring is constrained by page granularity and cannot fully record memory access traces. Leveraging the hardware page protection mechanism, we propose a byte-grained memory access monitoring method that does not require source code and offers improved performance. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, and after optimization runtime has been reduced by 9% on average.

articleTitle: Reversible Data Hiding for JPEG Images Based on Quantization-Table-Modification and STC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Reversible data hiding (RDH) for JPEG images has attracted extensive attentions in recent years. Particularly, quantized-DCT-coefficients-modification and quantization-table-modification are two main approaches for JPEG images RDH. However, for quantization-table-modification based methods, as lack of accurate measurement for the embedding distortion, its performance is far from optimal. Then, by incorporating syndrome-trellis-code (STC) into quantization-table-modification, a novel and efficient JPEG images RDH method is proposed in this paper. Specifically, by designing diverse reversible embedding rules with STC, the corresponding capacity-distortion model is established. In this way, the embedding distortion is well controlled, and the embedding performance is enhanced. Experimental results show that the proposed method can provide better visual quality compared with some state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Keyphrase Extraction Approach for Hazard Records by Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: During safety inspections, analyzing hazard records can help staff quickly assess the overall risk situation and formulate corrective measures. Key Phrase Extraction (KPE) can extract crucial phrases from documents with core information, aiding staff in conducting hazard record analysis. However, general SOTA approaches have performed poorly in security domains. In this study, we introduce a KPE method called Domain-oriented Joint Scores Rank, which evaluates and ranks candidate phrases by combining scores from multiple dimensions. Further, we have developed a security domain-oriented BERT model by proposing a lightweight comparative learning fine-tuning method. The HKBERT-based DJSRank outperforms the SOTA general domain model on the KPE task for hazard records, with an average F1 improvement of 4.3.

articleTitle: Research on Machine Learning-Assisted Pulse Discharge Plasma Catalysis for Methane-Carbon Dioxide Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Due to the substantial complexity of plasma numerical simulation processes and the significant time required for operation, this paper establishes a dedicated dataset. It investigates deep learning-assisted modeling methods for pulsed discharge plasma catalysis. By employing machine learning, we assess regression algorithms using K-fold cross-validation alongside the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) metrics. We select the most effective Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to assist in plasma catalysis modeling. Notably, the ANN demonstrates multiple advantages, including improved efficiency and adaptability. To enhance prediction accuracy, we implement Bayesian Optimization (BO) for tuning the ANN parameters. Experimental results indicate that the outcomes derived from the ANN, optimized through Bayesian methods, align well with the numerical results from dynamic models.

articleTitle: Optimizing SAR Target Detection Through the Multi-Stage Pre-Training and Fine-Tuning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) plays a crucial role in target detection due to its unique all-weather imaging capabilities. With the advancement of deep learning, numerous SAR target detection models have been proposed. However, the presence of speckle noise, low resolution, and the scarcity of SAR datasets have posed significant challenges to the training of these models. To address this issue, we propose a multi-stage pretraining-finetuning strategy. First, we pretrain the backbone on natural images, followed by fine-tuning the entire model on simulated SAR images, and finally fine-tuning it on real-world SAR data. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach effectively mitigates the gap between natural and SAR images, achieving superior results across various detection granularities.

articleTitle: Geosynchronous-Orbit-aided Low-Earth-Orbit Networking Management Mechanism for 6G Network Service Provisioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite networks have the advantages of low latency and high bandwidth compared to geosynchronous-orbit (GEO) satellites. However, their dynamic nature makes controlling satellite-terrestrial integration networks (STINs) a complex problem for 6G service. The traditional management architecture deploys SDN controllers in LEO satellites to realize multi-subdomain networking management. However, it is also challenging to guarantee latency and reliability of control message distribution due to the burstiness of network traffic and time-varying topology. To improve STIN’s control reliability and predictability, we propose a GEO-aided STIN management architecture, which can utilize the extensive coverage of GEO to achieve low-latency and high-reliability control. We built a STIN management simulation platform and conducted simulation validation in an LEO-GEO constellation network consisting of 144 LEO satellites and 3 GEO satellites. The results show that the proposed architecture can reduce the control latency and guarantee the stability of the control message under high-load cases.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Wafer Particle Defect Classification Based on Deep Learning and Multimodal Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: In the semiconductor manufacturing process, the identification and classification of the chemical composition of particle defects on wafers is critical to ensuring product quality. Traditional manual classification methods are affected by the operator's subjective judgement, which affects the accuracy and efficiency of classification. In this study, we propose a deep convolutional neural network (CNN)-based automatic defect classification model that fuses scanning electron microscope (SEM) images and energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectral data for more efficient and accurate defect identification.Our model first feeds the image data into a network with Residual Neural Network (ResNet-50) as the model backbone structure, which has learnt to recognise various types of defects through a large number of samples, and introduces a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) attention mechanism to the network, which aims to improve the network's ability to recognise defects. The attention mechanism is designed to enhance the network's capability to focus on and learn essential features. It employs a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to extract features from Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectra. Subsequently, the integration of image and spectral features is achieved through a multi-head self-attention mechanism. Finally, a fully connected layer is utilized to classify eight different types of defects within semiconductor particles.The experimental results show that our system improves the accuracy and processing speed of defect detection compared to traditional manual classification methods, and the comparison of the classification detection accuracy of different models for different input models is investigated.

articleTitle: TMAnet: An Innovative Approach for Classifying Motor Imagery EEG Signals Related to Motor Movements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: The Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) system utilizing Motor Imagery (MI) has diverse applications in medical rehabilitation. This study aims to validate the reliability of self-collected data and classify open-source electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. We introduce a temporal convolution network with multihead self-attention (TMAnet), designed for decoding EEG signals. This network combined with a data expansion approach based on cyclic translation strategy, which effectively expands experimental data without losing original information. To enhance the processing of self-collected signals, the EEG signals undergo the application of a spatio-temporal filtering technique and a low-rank approximation for generalized eigenvalue decomposition to effectively eliminate multiple artifacts. The proposed model could perform more accurate recognition of self-collected EEG signals than the existing methods, and the highest classification accuracy achieved was 83.75 on self-collected dataset. The effectiveness of this system was proven through the accurate classification of the self-collected MI EEG signals in this study.

articleTitle: ClassRAC: Leveraging Action Classification to Improve Repetitive Action Counting Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: The counting of repetitive actions is widely used in physical exercise for sports training and assessment. Existing methods have mainly concentrated on training models across multiple action classes, often neglecting the identification of specific action types. Building on previous experiments, we discovered that separating the training and validation datasets by action classes and conducting individual training and validation for each class can significantly enhance model performance. Inspired by this finding, we divide the task of repetitive action counting into two components: action classification and the optimization of counting algorithms for each action class. Specifically, we develop an action classification algorithm based on prior work, achieving an accuracy of 99.3% on the RepCount dataset. We also optimize the counting method for each action class, resulting in a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.146 and an Off-By-One (OBO) accuracy of 0.781 on the same dataset, which substantially surpasses the current state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Additionally, we introduce two preprocessing techniques tailored for action videos. Experiments confirm that these preprocessing methods effectively filter out irrelevant information, thereby improving counting accuracy.

articleTitle: Portfolio Optimization Based on Dynamic Multifactor Stock Scoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Current portfolio researches focus on the optimization model design and the risk measurement. Specifically, existing methods mainly utilize the return time series itself as an input, while factors describing various aspects of a stock’s state are not fully explored. Moreover, most current multifactor scoring models are linear, and may not adapt the complex market changes in a timely manner. Then, based on the above considerations, this paper presents a comprehensive investment model that seamlessly integrates stock selection and portfolio management into a cohesive framework. By incorporating fundamental and momentum factors, along with the predicted factor derived from technical factors, a nonlinear dynamic stock scoring method is proposed. These scores are then combined together to construct a portfolio optimization model. In this way, the portfolio returns are significantly improved, and the proposed advantages are experimentally verified compared to some state-of-the-art works.

articleTitle: A novel compact Chipless RFID Tag based on notched antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) tag using dual mode loop resonator (DMLR), open-loop resonator (OLR) and dual band-notched UWB antennas. 3N codes can be obtained by coupling N resonators of this kind with the microstrip. Through introducing the two band-notches on the UWB antenna, two more code bits can be performed without increasing the size of tag. Band notches on the antennas are designed in the lower frequency for high space efficiency. The simulated results are given and discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a RFID Antenna with Uniform Near-Field Distribution and Low Far-Field Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: A UHF RFID reader antenna for near-field applications is proposed in this paper which is based on two loop-ended microstrip (MS) meander lines. The antenna has six sections of MS meander line, two loop ends and one phase shifter, which is designed on a FR4. The permittivity of the substrate is 4.4mm and the thickness is 1 mm. The antenna size is 480 mm × 200 mm. Compared with the stub ends, the using of the loop ends achieves better uniform magnetic fields distribution. The simulated results are given and discussed.

articleTitle: Decoupling for Magneto-Electric Dipole MIMO Antenna Array by Using Meta-strip
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: A low coupling wideband magneto-electric (ME) dipole multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna array is proposed. The proposed array is composed of 8 ME dipole elements, ground plane, metal wall and meta-strips. Each ME dipole is designed under the ground plane and metal walls are constructed around the ME dipole, which is to increase the gain of each ME dipole. The designed meta-strips are modeled on the substrate which is loading under the proposed antenna array for decoupling between each ME dipole. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has achieved -10-dB fractional bandwidth of 24% (4.4-5.6 GHz) and realized low coupling (less than -18 dB) over the achieved bandwidth. Mover, the proposed antenna array has gained good directional property.

articleTitle: Analysis of Safety Warning for the Transportation of Flammable Solids by Railway
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: To further enhance the safety of railway transportation of hazardous goods, this paper takes the transportation of flammable solids by railway as an example to study the safety risk factors in the transportation process, providing insights for safety warning. Firstly, the entire transportation process is analyzed using the Hazard and Operability Analysis (HAZOP) method to identify safety risk factors in the transportation process, which serve as the basis for actual production operations. Secondly, combined with rough set theory, the obtained safety risk factors are screened to eliminate redundant factors that do not contribute significantly to safe transportation and extract core factors. Finally, based on the core factors, a safety warning index system for the transportation process of flammable solid substances is constructed, and the principles of safety warning operations are elaborated to provide reference for safety warning in the actual transportation production process.

articleTitle: Print-Resilient Binary Image Watermarking Based on Grayscale Conversion and DCT Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Current binary image watermarking methods are mainly spatial domain methods, and most of them cannot resist printing and scanning. Based on this consideration, this paper introduces a new print-resilient watermarking method tailored for binary images. For data embedding, by dividing the cover binary image into disjoint blocks and counting the black pixels in each block, it is first converted into a form similar to a grayscale image. Then, by applying DCT to the transformed image, two DCT coefficients are selected and modified to embed the watermark. Next, after modification, the transformed image is converted back to the spatial domain to identify the number of pixels that need to be changed in each binary image block. Finally, for the cover binary image, edge detection is employed to select and modify its pixels (white to black, or black to white) without reducing the image quality, effectively realizing the watermark embedding. Experimental results show that the proposed method can well preserve the visual quality while resist the print-scan attack.

articleTitle: A Broadband Circularly Polarized Filtering Patch Antenna with Stacked Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: A double-layer stacked patch filtering antenna with broadband circular polarization performance is proposed in this paper. The main patch consists of a corner-truncated square patch with two shorting pins. The designed two shorting pins are located in the main patch and the upper stacked patch structure are introduced and designed, which can gain two radiation nulls for realizing the filtering effect of the proposed antenna. The circularly polarized (CP) operation is realized by corner-truncated square patch. In addition, to increase the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth, a rectangular slot is carved on the ground plane. The simulated results indicate that the researched antenna can provide the impedance bandwidth of 20.58% (2.68-3.29 GHz) and AR bandwidth of 9.5% (2.80-3.08 GHz). Moreover, The average realized gain of the simulation is 6.48 dBic over bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Pillar-based Lightweight 3D Detector with Density-Enhanced Pillar Encoder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: To address the challenges in the field of 3D object detection, such as complex network architectures, large network parameter counts, and the prevalent use of sparse convolution which is not conducive to edge deployment, we design a lightweight and real-time 3D object detection neural network, which consists of three parts. In the pillar encoding section of the network, we resolve the issue of insufficient point cloud data within some pillars, which makes element-wise feature aggregation difficult, by introducing a Density-Enhanced Pillar Encoding module (DEPE). DEPE expands the perceptual range of distant pillars based on density information, allowing them to include more potential neighboring points and more fully leverage the feature extraction capabilities of the pillar encoding module, without significantly increasing computational load. In the backbone of the network, in line with the requirements for lightweight and real-time performance, we utilize reparameterization techniques and depth-wise separable convolutions, enabling the backbone to have the advantages of a single branch and fewer parameters during inference, while also avoiding the use of sparse convolution and thereby reducing the difficulty of network deployment on edge devices. Experiments on the KITTI dataset demonstrate that our proposed method offers significant advantages in terms of parameters and inference latency, with a mere 1.87M parameters and an inference frame rate of up to 18Hz, achieving a balance between efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: UWSNs Deployment Method Based on Sink Node Gravitational Pull and Dynamic Communication Radius
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: In response to the issues of low actual coverage and poor network connectivity in underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) node deployment, and considering the potential hotspot problem that may arise from uniform deployment optimization, this paper proposes a node deployment method based on sink node gravitational pull and dynamic communication radius. Through simulation verification, the proposed method achieves a high coverage rate and minimizes the number of disconnected nodes under conditions with 50, 100, 150, and 200 nodes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Problems of Electromagnetic System Engineering of Polar Ships
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: This paper primarily examines the challenges posed by snow, ice, and low temperatures in polar environments on the design of ship electronic equipment, specifically how these factors hinder the normal functioning of onboard radar, communication, and navigation systems. In response to these technical issues, the paper proposes targeted recommendations to mitigate their impact.

articleTitle: A Dense Network Model of Traffic Classification Based on Autoencoder and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: To address the problems of poor effect of feature dimensionality reduction, gradient disappearance and inadequate extraction of features from different layers in existing models of network traffic classification, a dense network model of traffic classification based on auto-encoder combined with attention mechanism is proposed. The proposed model firstly adopts auto-encoder to better achieve dimensionality reduction of data feature. Secondly, the model introduces the attention mechanism to increase the weight of features that have an important impact on the classification performance. Finally, it achieves multi-layer feature reuse by introducing DenseNet, a dense connection network, and then improves feature learning capability by shortening the connection between the front and back layers. The proposed classification model is trained and validated using the CIC2018 dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed model achieves a certain magnitude of improvement in traffic classification performance relative to the existing classification model.

articleTitle: Kernel Weibull M-transform Least Mean Square Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: The paper introduces a Kernel Weibull M-transform Least-Mean Square (LMS) (KWMLMS) algorithm aimed to enhance filtering performance for a nonlinear system. By incorporating the Weibull M-transformation into the cost function of the Kernel LMS (KLMS) algorithm, a weighting updated rule is gotten. Simulation experiments conducted for nonlinear-system identification under impulse noise conditions demonstrate that the created KWMLMS algorithm achieves significantly faster convergence compared to existing methods, indicating its superiority in dealing with impulsive-noises.

Author Keywords: Weibull M-transform Least Mean Square algorithm

articleTitle: Photo Response Non-Uniformity Based AI-Generated Image Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: The hyper-realism of images generated by diffusion models has become increasingly impressive, making it difficult for humans to distinguish between AI-generated and real images. Most existing detectors rely on extracting artifacts inherent in the process of creating fake images, often ignoring the unique fingerprints left behind when real images are captured. It has been observed that real images exhibit a distinctive pattern noise known as Photo Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU). Based on this consideration, in this study, an Al-generated image detection method based on PRNU is proposed. Specifically, by combining PRNU features with original image features, we effectively capture the intrinsic noise patterns in real images and then train a classification network. Experimental results on 11 generative models demonstrate the practical effectiveness of this method in detecting AI-generated images.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement Based on Improved Water-net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Complex underwater environments and scarce real-world training datasets pose substantial obstacles to underwater image enhancement models based on Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN). In this paper, we first optimize the main network framework for the Water-net baseline model by selecting two convolutional blocks that differ only in the number of channels to be learned. Then in the convolution block connection process, we concatenate the original input with the convolutional output to enhance feature integration. For fusion, three different and more advantageous preprocessing methods are selected and increases the AquaBlend ConvModule (ABCM) enhancement module to enhance output quality while preventing overfitting. The improved model shows intentional performance on the full reference metrics, which is significantly improved compared to the baseline model, and the effectiveness of our method is verified in experiments on diverse underwater datasets.

articleTitle: Class Activation Mapping-guided Delineation of ROI in Medical Images for Automatic Local Contrast Enhancement in Lateral Cervical Spine Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Clinical reading of lateral cervical spine radiographs often requires manual adjustment of contrast to highlight the characteristics of the regions of interest. Automatic enhancement schemes can replace manual labor but often introduce issues including over-enhancement, under-enhancement, increased background noise, and an inability to separate Region of Interest (ROI) from the complex-structured background. This study proposes an identification and enhancement scheme for regions of interest in lateral cervical spine radiographs. First, a target detector for the regions of C1-C7 vertebrae was trained on 1,000 images. Utilizing the explanatory power of the HiResCAM on convolutional neural networks, Class Activation Mapping of shallow features was employed to automatically delineate the vertebrae regions. Subsequently, local contrast enhancement was conducted to improve the readability of the vertebral areas while avoiding the amplification of background noise. Pixel-level alpha blending was applied at the edges of the ROI to eliminate the boundaries between regions. Experimental results on real medical images demonstrate that this method significantly enhances the readability of the vertebral areas in lateral cervical spine images without damaging peripheral information, surpassing previous approaches with its human-like focus on the local ROIs.

Index Terms: Lateral Radiographs Of The Cervical Spine

articleTitle: Study on Lidar Pulse Timing Method Based on Pulse Width Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: For the sensitivity of analog timing to clutter in the existing pulse lidar system, this paper proposes a laser pulse timing method based on pulse width compensation. This method uses the pulse width information of the laser radar pulse to confirm the timing time. The simulation results show that compared with the leading adge timing method and the constant fraction timing method, the proposed method has better calculation accuracy, especially with the low SNR, which is beneficial to improve the ranging performance of the lidar system.

articleTitle: Beam Spatial Arrangement in Two-Dimensional Phased Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: This paper analyzes the beam spatial arrangement of two-dimensional phased array radar. It defines the coordinate systems involved in beam arrangement, examines the coordinate transformations, and conducts simulation calculations based on engineering design. The findings provide a reference for optimizing radar beam spatial arrangement.

articleTitle: Accelerating Power Big Data Queries by Binary Partitioning and Workload-Driven Pre-joins
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Querying power big data across multiple sections plays an important role in achieving efficient power data sharing and emergent accident handling. However, power big data often suffers from the issues of data sparsity and low query efficiency. In this paper, we propose a power big data query acceleration method based on binary partitioning and workload-driven pre-joins (BP-WPJ). First, the original power property tables can be vertically partitioned into multiple binary tables (BTs) for eliminating null-value elements, producing the statistics of data type frequency in BTs. Second, a workload-driven pre-join processing method (WPJ) is proposed to identify the join patterns of the query statement in terms of predicates and join relations. Third, we optimize the order of query triples by dividing the query statement into multiple query triples based on the bounded elements for accelerating power data query. Experiments were made on three datasets compared to three popular methods, and the results show that BP-WPJ is very competitive against the three baselines. It can significantly accelerate big data query and achieves relatively lower memory consumption, thereby meeting the practical needs of power big data queries.

articleTitle: Research on the Characterization Method of Lidar Echo Pulse Intensity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: LiDAR echo intensity data records the radiation characteristics and surface roughness of the target object. The use of echo intensity data for effective target recognition and extraction has gradually become a research hotspot in the field of LiDAR signal processing. This article analyzes and compares several commonly used methods for recording LiDAR echo intensity data, derives the theoretical formulas for each method's LiDAR echo intensity recording method, and conducts actual experimental verification. The experimental results indicate that the intensity data obtained by the waveform centroid recording method shows a clear linear distribution trend with the target reflectivity, with a small standard deviation and high robustness.

articleTitle: Research on the Acceptance Behavior of Accounting Professionals towards Large Language Models and Generative Artificial Intelligence: An Analysis Based on ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI), such as ChatGPT, permeates into our lives, its unparalleled application value has been showcased. This study delves into the accounting domain, examining professionals' acceptance behavior towards large language models (LLMs) and generative AI. Six hypotheses were proposed, and an initial technology acceptance model was developed based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was employed to assess the research model, utilizing data from an empirical survey of 451 accounting professionals in China. The findings suggest that acceptance behavior is primarily influenced by perceived risk, personal innovation, community influence, and technological advancements. Notably, the moderating factor does not significantly impact usage intention.

Author Keywords: unified theory of acceptance and use of technology

articleTitle: Teleoperation of a Roach Cyborg Equipped with Microphone and Minicamera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: The paper describes how to construct small lightweight stimulation module, microphone, and mini camera using cockroach as a platform, as well as how to integrates these independently working modules into an electronic backpack. In addition, an ejector is designed to launch the microphone and mini camera according to instructions. The software and hardware design is conducted according to the functional requirements of each module in the electronic backpack, resulting in a cockroach cyborg that can be remotely controlled with the assistance of a mini camera and has the ability to deliver audio/video sensors after finding targets.

articleTitle: A Novel Audio Forgery Detection Method Based on Short-time Power Spectral Density
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: The popularity of portable recording equipment has made the acquisition of digital audio convenient, and the development of multimedia editing software has made audio editing and modification progressively easier. Therefore, it is essential to ensure the authenticity and integrity of digital media files. Copy-move forgery is a prevalent form of audio tampering, but existing detection methods suffer from low accuracy and poor robustness. To address this issue, we propose a detection method for audio copy-move forgery based on short-time power spectral density (STPSD). Specifically, we first separate the syllables in the voiced part of the speech signal. Then, the STPSD features are extracted from the suspect byte pair. Finally, the content matching algorithm is used for detection. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can resist all kinds of common attacks reliably, and can accurately locate copied and moved forged syllables, with high efficiency.

articleTitle: A Phase Noise Immune Equalization Algorithm For Millimeter Wave SC-FDE System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: To solve the problem that phase noise affection of high-order modulation in millimeter wave broadband system, this paper analyzes and modifies the theoretical model of phase noise provided in the 802.11ad and 802.15.3c standards, and generates the actual noise values based on the modified model for simulation analysis. The frame structure given in standards is optimized for SC-FDE system to estimate noise and channel state by adding data block 0. An improved MMSE equalization algorithm is proposed in this paper to track the channel and phase noise changes in real time and obvious phase noise immunity characteristic is obtained compared with traditional algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on EMC Evaluation and Management Method Based on Time-Frequency Domain and Complex Network Modeling Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: This paper proposes an electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) evaluation and management method based on time-frequency domain analysis and complex networks, which can be used to evaluate the EMC of complex systems with multiple frequency equipment and provide recommendations for electromagnetic management methods. First, time-frequency domain processing methods are used to process electromagnetic environment (EME) data or conduct time-frequency domain simulation analysis on the equipment installed on the platform in typical working modes to sort out its time-frequency characteristics. Secondly, combining the application of complex network theory in the field of EMC, and taking into account the interference situation between equipment in the time-frequency domain, an overall EMC evaluation is conducted, and corresponding management method suggestions are given based on the evaluation results. Finally, through simulation analysis of the example, the method proposed in this paper can better evaluate the EMC of complex platforms or systems, and reduce the impact on electromagnetic spectrum resources and equipment utilization during EMC management.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multi-feature Attention Neural Tree for EEG-based Fatigue Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Driver fatigue assessment is important to traffic safety, and the gold standard for fatigue detection is widely regarded as the EEG signals. Traditional machine learning methods fall short in accurately identifying EEG signals, while deep learning methods, though highly accurate, often lack model interpretability. This paper introduces an Adaptive Multi-feature Attention Neural Tree (AMANT) for fatigue signal recognition, leveraging the spatial structure of EEG signals. Initially, the EEG time series signal is converted into a two-dimensional matrix that preserves the information on channel positions and spatial details. Subsequently, a channel attention mechanism is applied, allowing the module to adaptively adjust the significance of each frequency, thereby enhancing the model's expressive capability. The AMANT integrates neural network modeling with decision tree technology, offering improved model interpretability. Experiments conducted on the SEED-VIG dataset achieved an average accuracy of 96.38%(DE) and 96.85%(PSD), with fewer model parameters and statistically significant results, thereby verifying the efficacy of the proposed approach. AMANT facilitates the automatic exploration of suitable network architectures, feature extraction, and end-to-end training while providing model interpretability. It effectively combines the strengths of traditional machine learning with deep learning, offering a robust solution for fatigue recognition.

articleTitle: A Novel Quantum Dandelion Reproduction Optimization Algorithm for solving Low-carbon FJSP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Faced with complex and ever-changing market demands, enterprises not only need to meet customer needs by providing better products and services to maximize their overall efficiency, but also need to adjust their production strategies to achieve energy conservation and emission reduction. Considering that the dandelion algorithm is not easily trapped in local optima and has strong robustness, a solution strategy based on the dandelion reproduction algorithm is proposed in this paper, but the algorithm drifting down operation adopts a fixed step size, and the wandering search near the optimal position consumes too long a time, which will result in the loss of dandelion individuals that have a high degree of adaptability. Combining the properties of quantum state entanglement, superposition and interference, this paper further proposes Hybrid Quantum Dandelion Reproduction Optimization Algorithm (HQDRO). The performance of the algorithm is verified and comparatively analyzed through the classical examples of workshop scheduling, and the results show that the use of HQDRO to solve the low-carbon FJSP problem not only improves the convergence speed of the algorithm, obtains high-quality feasible solutions quickly, but also provides an effective solution to the FJSP problem.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Sidechain Security and Efficiency: A Restaking and Contract Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Sidechain technology aids in building lightweight and rapid-response blockchain services in resource limited Internet of Things (IoT) environments, yet the low trust model of sidechains is a concern. The restaking mechanism offers a way to aggregate mainchain trust on sidechains. Inspired by this, our paper introduces a security reuse solution suitable for IoT sidechains. Addressing the principal-agent problems aggravated by information asymmetry and restaking mechanism in IoT sidechain networks, we propose a solution strategy based on contract theory and exemption limits. The feasibility and effectiveness of this approach are confirmed through simulation analysis. Our work contribute to advancing a more secure, efficient, and decentralized approach to integrating IoT and blockchain.

articleTitle: Research on Low-Resource Neural Machine Translation Methods Based on Explicit Sparse Attention and Pre-trained Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: The development of machine translation is driven by the need for global communication through the automatic translation of words, sentences, and texts from one language to another. This paper proposes an improved Transformer-based model to enhance the performance of Kazakh-English machine translation and explores its feasibility and advantages in this field.The Transformer model, with its self-attention mechanism, has demonstrated state-of-the-art performance across various natural language processing tasks. While self-attention effectively captures long-range dependencies, it may extract irrelevant information from the context. To address this issue, we propose an algorithm called the Explicit Sparse Attention (ESA) algorithm. The sparse attention mechanism enhances focus on the global context by selecting the most relevant segments. In addition, a general form of attention enhancement for Transformer models is introduced, which allows for the integration of pre-trained language models and facilitates the modeling of word order relations between source and target languages.Experimental results, using publicly available datasets provided by the official bilingual websites of the Kazakhstan government (The Republic of Kazakhstan, 2023; Strategy, 2022; Primeminister, 2022), show that the proposed model achieves a BLEU score of 0.51, WER of 0.50, and TER of 0.43. The proposed model demonstrates significant advantages in the Kazakh-English low-resource translation field and achieves notable improvements over recent advancements in this domain.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Survival Prediction for Breast Cancer Using Multi-Modal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: In the current medical field, survival prediction for breast cancer patients has increasingly relied on multimodal data, driven by rapid advancements in medical imaging technology and genomics. These developments provide clinicians with more precise treatment options, improving patient survival rates. However, existing studies often neglect the inherent discrepancies between different data modalities and struggle to effectively integrate multi-modal features. To address these challenges, this paper presents a survival prediction framework for breast cancer based on multi-modal data. By incorporating three distinct data modalities, the framework aims to minimize inter-modality discrepancies and effectively integrate multi-modal features to enhance survival prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a strong concordance index (C-index) of 0.707.

articleTitle: Design of a Wide Band Antenna with Cross-Finger Structure for Covering 2.6GHz-20GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: A wide band antenna element is designed to achieve 3-20 GHz wideband impedance matching and its performance is investigated herein. By employing a modified cross-finger structure and two resistive frequency selective surfaces (RFSS), the antenna impedance matching has been improved, where the presented cross-finger structure is functioned as a coupling capacitor to mitigate inductive effects. Also, two resistive frequency selective surfaces are used for effectively improving the matching and reducing the Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) at specific frequencies, which are well designed according to the required frequencies. Simulation result indicates that the VSWR is less than 2 within the frequency range of 2.65 to 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Visual SLAM Based on Geometric Constraints and Lightweight Object Detection Network in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: In dynamic environments, performing Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is often disrupted by moving objects, resulting in decreased localization accuracy and robustness. This paper proposes a dynamic feature point elimination algorithm based on geometric constraints and an object detection network. By using only static feature points in the camera pose calculation, the algorithm processes images captured by visual sensors, effectively enhancing the system's localization accuracy and robustness in dynamic scenes. Additionally, to address the issues of large parameter sizes and the difficulty of meeting SLAM's real-time requirements in current object detection networks, this paper presents a lightweight improvement of YOLO-V5s. In the TUM dynamic scene dataset, the improved algorithm achieves a 95.29% increase in localization accuracy compared to ORB-SLAM2 and processes 13.5 frames per second, meeting the real-time requirements of visual SLAM.

articleTitle: YOLO: An Improved High-Accuracy Method for PCB Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Throughout the manufacturing process of printed circuit boards (PCBs), any flaws on the surface can negatively affect the quality of the product, leading to potential issues with equipment performance stability and reliability. Small defects are rare in PCBs, making their features weak and easily affected by background interference, which makes detection difficult. To tackle the issue, this study proposes the VSP-YOLO model. By introducing the VSConv feature extraction module, which combines RepVGG blocks and space-to-depth (SPD) technology, the model optimizes information extraction and retention processes. Inspired by RepVGG's multi-path structure and SPD's spatial segmentation, VSConv effectively captures and retains information related to small defects. Moreover, the model employs the Sequential Polarized Self-Attention (SPSA) mechanism in the detection head to enhance target recognition while removing the detection head used for large targets, thereby reducing the parameter count. Experimental results demonstrate that the VSP-YOLO model achieves an average precision mAP@0.5 of 97.9% and a mAP@0.5:0.95 of 62.14% in detecting small targets and high-resolution images, respectively. Compared to the traditional YOLOv8 model, the VSP-YOLO model improves performance by 2.4% and 3.5%, respectively, while reducing parameters by 23% and achieving a frame rate of 136 frames per second (FPS).

articleTitle: An Encrypted Traffic Classification Model Based on Improved Dense Network and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of incomplete data feature extraction and long training time in the current encrypted traffic classification model, an encrypted traffic classification model based on improved densely connected network and bidirectional gated recurrent unit is proposed. The model first uses one-dimensional convolution and LeakyReLU in the dense connection part to improve the learning ability of neurons, extract the spatial features of the data and reduce the training time of the model; then a bidirectional gated recurrent unit is added to extract the complete time series features of the data; Finally, the data features extracted by the two modules are fused and input into the classifier to complete the traffic classification. The experimental results show that the classification accuracy of the improved model is 96.4%, the accuracy rate is 96.8%, and the recall rate is 96.6% in the classification of complex types of encrypted traffic. Compared with the existing models, the performances of improved model are improved.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in UAV-assisted Mobile Edge Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: In a crowdsensing system, effective transmission of sensing data is an important step in improving task distribution efficiency. In real-life scenarios, when resources are limited or geographic conditions are harsh, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) can often be used for data transmission. This paper proposes a group intelligence sensing task distribution method under dynamic topology conditions to solve the problems of unreachable links or high network overhead caused by the dynamic topology of UAVs. This method uses the Markov model to model the data transmission process, and on this basis proposes an improved task distribution method based on topology awareness to achieve efficient task forwarding. The final experimental results show that compared with the traditional self-organizing network data transmission scheme for opportunistic networks, the scheme proposed in this paper can better solve the problems of routing voids and blind paths, and effectively improve the network lifetime while realizing a lower end-to-end delay, with better transmission performance.

articleTitle: Bi-Criteria Optimization for Balancing Communication Connectivity and Distance Based on β-DQN in UAV Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computer Science and Network Technology (ICCSNT)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) offer significant advantages in maritime search and rescue by covering vast ocean areas rapidly. However, the complex maritime environment and limited communication coverage often necessitate multi-hop communication to maintain connectivity with the Ground Control Station (GCS). Optimizing UAV flight paths to minimize communication interruptions and reduce flight distance is crucial for conserving energy and time. This paper introduces the β-DQN algorithm, an enhancement of the traditional DQN algorithm, designed to optimize both communication connectivity and flight distance. The reward structure is divided into two parts: one for actions before reaching the destination, incorporating decay for faster convergence, and another for achieving the optimal path. This approach innovatively introduces the communication interruption penalty index β, modeled as a piecewise function that accounts for both communication penalties and distance-related rewards. Simulations show that β-DQN converges faster, with shorter paths and better connectivity than DQN. This reward design approach can also be applied to other reinforcement learning algorithms for improved bi-criteria path planning.
